column1: # DOC_GATE_ALIAS_REACH.tsv - GATE 18 (scripts/doc_gates.sh alias-reach)
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The most-repeated finding of the adversarial review campaign
# (~30 passes) has one shape: a correct ruling gets applied to ONE line and nothing
# detects the gap. CITATIONS.md's item-3 parenthetical rules that "C1+C2+C3" in older
# text is legacy naming for the C1-C5 canonical (see METHODS §"Legacy shorthand") and
# that "exhaustive" is corrected to "budgeted" - and at the time this gate was written,
# CITATIONS.md line 85 of the SAME FILE still carried both uncorrected forms, and no
# document that uses the aliases linked the ruling. The existing gates catch forbidden
# text PRESENT; this registry drives the gate for the opposite class: required
# resolution ABSENT, i.e. a live use of a ruled alias that is not within one link of
# the ruling that resolves it.
# WHAT COUNTS AS "WITHIN ONE LINK", mechanically: the use's OWN LINE either carries the
# rule's resolution token (a fixed substring that only a line narrating or citing the
# ruling would carry - e.g. the METHODS section name), or is covered by an explicit
# content-anchored `allow` row below. File-granular reach ("the note is linked SOMEWHERE
# in this file") was considered and rejected: CITATIONS.md carries the ruling at one
# line and the defect 438 lines above it, which is exactly the gap this gate exists to
# see. Line-granular is the strict-but-honest reading, and the cost is this curated file.
# SCOPE OF JURISDICTION. This registry is for "read X as Y" / legacy-naming /
# supersession rulings where X may legitimately remain in the corpus in another sense.
# Retracted PHRASES (text that should not appear at all) belong in
# RETRACTED_PHRASES.tsv (GATE 3); retracted FIGURES in RETRACTED_FIGURES.tsv (GATE 3b).
# The distinguishing test: if every occurrence of X is wrong, register it there; if X
# has a live legitimate sense that must NOT be "corrected" (both aliases below do),
# register it here, because only a content-anchored classification can avoid punishing
# the legitimate sense.
# ATTRIBUTION CORRECTIONS (`attrib` rows, 2026-08-06) are the second class under this
# registry's jurisdiction, and the distinguishing test above decides their placement:
# a superseded attribution is wrong at EVERY live claim site (which smells like
# GATE 3), but the only detectable string is the PERSON'S NAME, and the name has live
# legitimate senses — the correction's own narration, dated revision-history records
# (append-only; rewriting them would falsify the record), and the person cited for a
# distinct, still-supported contribution. GATE 3's one-file-substring exemption cannot
# express those classes, has no [OPEN] backlog, and its own history (four rows for one
# hard-floor claim, variants still escaping) shows claim-phrase rows are evasion-shaped
# where name-keyed rows are not. So: the name is registered HERE, and the exemption
# classes carry the semantics. What an unexempted hit means differs from an alias hit —
# a dead credit restated, not an unresolved shorthand — so `attrib` rows print their
# own [FAIL] wording.
# WHAT `attrib` ROWS CANNOT CATCH, stated: a nameless restatement of the dead claim
# ("the 12th-century identification of the split") carries no registered string.
# SIBLINGS SWEPT AT SEEDING (2026-08-06), recorded so the absence of rows for them is
# a finding and not an omission — each was checked corpus-wide and its superseded form
# no longer appears, so there is nothing for a rule to adjudicate and a name-keyed rule
# would cost hundreds of curated rows for zero live defects:
#   * Cook-as-primary for the gender/position-parity rule (corrected 2026-07-03 to
#     Schulz 1990; CITATIONS.md §Attributed, TR-6:94, TR-1:269): every surviving site
#     says Schulz-primary / Cook-elaborated or co-lists them for the class convention.
#   * biroco.com attributed to "Steve Moore" (corrected 2026-07-19 to S. J. Marshall;
#     CITATIONS.md #marshall-biroco): no surviving misattribution; legacy anchor
#     `moore-biroco` is deliberate and documented in the entry.
#   * Meyer's priority for the two first-order-difference properties (withdrawn
#     2026-08-01, credited to McKenna & McKenna 1975; CITATIONS.md #meyer1998): all
#     surviving Meyer credits are the retained scopes (the cyclic sequence AS DATA,
#     the 1993 timewave appendix, the Timewave-software critique relay).
#   * CX-23's five researcher-statement corrections are enforced by GATE 3 (their
#     superseded forms are fixed PHRASES with a single narrating file — GATE 3's exact
#     shape), and were left there deliberately.
# If a future correction's superseded form is LIVE anywhere, seed an `attrib` row then.
# THE TWO-SENSE TRAP, stated because it is the false-positive mode that kills gates:
# "C1+C2+C3" has TWO live senses - (a) the legacy alias for the C1-C5 canonical
# population ("the C1+C2+C3 canonical", "706M orderings under C1+C2+C3"), and (b) the
# literal three-predicate conjunction ("no null family simultaneously satisfies
# C1+C2+C3" - a statement about C1, C2 and C3 individually, where the C1-C5 canonical
# is not the object). Sense (b) must never fire and must never be "fixed": rewriting it
# to C1-C5 would introduce an error. Sense (b) occurrences are `allow` rows with class
# `literal`. Likewise "exhaustive enumeration" has a legitimate hypothetical/contrast
# sense ("under true exhaustive enumeration both partitions would converge") and a
# legitimate finite-complete sense ("exhaustive enumeration of all 2^27 circuits");
# the DEFECT sense is the definite-article NAMING of the actual budgeted runs ("the
# exhaustive enumeration cannot state an exact total"). The registered fixed string for
# that rule is therefore "the exhaustive enumeration" (case-folded), which at seeding
# time separated the two senses with zero curated exemptions: every legitimate use in
# the corpus is article-less or "under"-governed.
# WHAT THIS GATE CANNOT CATCH, stated rather than left to be rediscovered:
#   * article-less naming uses of "exhaustive enumeration" for the actual runs -
#     TR11_EXACT_COUNTING_BY_SYMMETRY_QUOTIENT.md:45 "alongside exhaustive enumeration
#     (exact lower bounds; TR-3)" and CITATIONS.md:995 "or exhaustive enumeration.
#     [analyzed]" are live borderline sites the fixed string cannot reach without
#     swallowing the hypothetical-contrast sense corpus-wide. They are recorded here
#     as prose (this comment) and belong to task #146's fix pass, not to a wider
#     pattern.
#   * a line carrying BOTH senses of an alias is classified as ONE line: exemption and
#     adjudication are line-granular (GATE 3b's model). CRITIQUE.md's "Simultaneous
#     C1+C2+C3 satisfaction..." line carries a literal use AND an alias use; it is
#     adjudicated `open` for the alias half, and its `allow literal` row below takes
#     over only once the alias half is fixed and the open row deleted.
#   * aliases nobody registered. The registry is the gate's eyes; a new ruling that is
#     recorded in CORRECTIONS.md/CITATIONS.md but never seeded here is invisible.
# OPEN ROWS ARE OPEN DEFECTS, NOT EXEMPTIONS - same contract as
# DOC_GATE_FIGURE_LEDGER_OPEN.txt: every `open` row is re-printed as [OPEN] on every
# run, with a count, so the backlog can never quietly become invisible. Fixing the
# underlying text is an adjudication owned by task #146 (corpus-wide propagation of
# the two alias rulings) or task #157 (the Zheng Qiao attribution sites - each `open`
# row names its owner), not a gate change. TO CLOSE an open row: fix the line (say C1-C5 /
# budgeted, or add a same-line pointer to the ruling), then DELETE the row here; a row
# whose anchor no longer matches anything is re-printed as [note] every run - the
# drift audit - so a stale row cannot sit here unnoticed. A NEW unadjudicated use
# fails the build from the day this gate shipped.
# FORMAT (tab-separated; first field selects the row kind; unknown kinds are a [FAIL],
# not a skip - a malformed row must not silently stop being enforced):
#   rule  <alias> <mode:exact|nocase> <stopchars or -> <resolution token> <where the ruling lives> <the ruling, one line>
#         mode nocase = both line and alias are case-folded before the fixed-string
#         search (no regex). stopchars: an occurrence immediately followed by one of
#         these characters is VOID - "C1+C2+C3" followed by "+" is the explicit
#         conjunction C1+C2+C3+C4(+C5), which is not the alias and must not fire.
#   attrib <name> <mode:exact|nocase> <stopchars or -> <resolution token> <where the correction lives> <the correction, one line>
#         same field layout and same detection as `rule`; the kind records that this is
#         a SUPERSEDED ATTRIBUTION (see the jurisdiction note above), so an unexempted
#         hit is reported as a dead credit restated, not an unresolved alias.
#   allow <file> <alias> <same-line anchor> <class> <why>
#         content-anchored, GATE 3b's shape - no line numbers, they drift. class is one
#         of: resolution-note (the ruling's own body text), literal (sense (b) above),
#         historical (a dated record, true when written; rewriting would falsify it),
#         meta-mention (quotes the alias in the act of discussing/recording it),
#         other-contribution (`attrib` rows only in intent: the person is cited for a
#         DISTINCT, still-supported claim - the superseded credit is not on the line;
#         requires the distinct claim to have its own bibliographic support, which is
#         why CRITIQUE.md's trigram-clustering mention is `open` and not here: the
#         bibliography's only remaining Zheng Qiao content is the correction itself).
#         Anything else is a [FAIL]: the class vocabulary is closed so the exemption
#         mechanism cannot silently widen.
#   open  <file> <alias> <same-line anchor> <what is open / who owns the fix>
rule
